chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:
I asked him about the salat over the deceased. He said: Five takbirs; then when you have finished them, you give salām to your right.
So the interpretation of this narration is taqiyyah, because it agrees with the doctrines of the generality.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity to protect oneself in hostile conditions
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ عَلَى الْمَيِّتِ: the funeral salat performed over the deceased
key_terms.خَمْسُ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ: five declarations of takbīr in the funeral prayer
key_terms.سَلَّمْتَ: you give salām as a concluding greeting
key_terms.مَذَاهِبِ الْعَامَّةِ: the legal views of the Sunni majority

ai.seo_question: Is there a salām in the funeral salat, or is this narration understood as taqiyyah?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of salat over the deceased, mentioning five takbirs and a salām to the right after completing them. The closing statement explains that this particular narration is understood as having been issued in taqiyyah because its ruling conforms to the views of the generality rather than the established Shia position of the chapter.
